message.content:
Introduction

The rapid development of artificial intelligence (including (systems (that (perform [well {in low-data} conditions]) (where (data (are scarce)))))) has raised important questions about evaluation, governance, and the limits of current systems. This paper situates those questions within a broader research context: as AI systems become more autonomous, scalable, and embedded in decision-making processes, the need for rigorous, transparent, and ethically grounded assessment becomes increasingly urgent. We argue that progress in AI requires not only technical benchmarking but also careful attention to reliability, interpretability, and long-term societal consequences. The remainder of this introduction outlines the scope of the paper, reviews key lines of work, and previews the contributions that follow.
